records.c: Disables interrupts and the display, installs the ending IRQ at line $10, sets up six sprites and configures VIC bank $C000 for the bitmap presentation. Copies graphics under the I/O area before restoring $01 to $35.

Opens RAM under I/O. Copies bitmap rows from $D000 and $B800 into $E800–$FEFF, then copies the final 64-byte slice from $BF00 to $FF00. Moves the bank-$C000 workspace, restores I/O, and enters the colour-cell copy.
Copies four overlapping source slices beginning at $B3E8 to the C64 colour-RAM window after restoring access to I/O.
Clears the ending sequence counters and background colours, sets up the text display state and starts the music through $5500 with selector one. Enables interrupts before making the scene visible.
Waits for the IRQ-side code to set $955A before running the fixed delay loops and moving to the next ending phase.
Sets the visible flag at $9163 through the shared following code, then waits for two IRQ acknowledgments through $59.
Clears the visible flag at $9163, then uses the same two acknowledgments.
Copies X complete pages from source high byte A to destination high byte Y. Patches both high-byte operands and increments them after each 256-byte copy.
First raster handler installed at $908F-$9092.
Clears the display acknowledgment, changes the common sprite colours, and builds four sprite coordinates from a base position at $9161/$9162 before writing their pointers and VIC registers.
Reads the next message item at $9563. Zero sets $9559, $FE toggles an animation bit and continues fetching, space maps to $1C, and $FF maps to $1B. The selected glyph index is masked to six bits.
Iterates through five text areas selected by pointer tables at $95C7 and $95CC and clears 48 bytes at each. Also prepares the VIC colour entries using a self-modified address.
Masks used by $91C8 and $9276 to set an individual sprite's high X bit.
Character and control bytes consumed at $93D6. $FE toggles the animation bit and continues, while zero signals the message end.
Installs the IRQ at $96BB and disables sprites. Clears bitmap RAM backwards beginning at $FF3F before selecting entries from the scene tables.
The first 1000 bytes are the screen colour attributes for the bitmap. $90E9 copies the four pages beginning here to screen RAM at $C000.
Colour RAM source at $90F2. The copy loop writes the four spans beginning at $D800, $D900, $DA00 and $DAE8.
First 1024 bytes of the bitmap slice copied from $B800 to $F800 by $90CC.
Remainder of the bitmap source slice beginning at $B800. The last 64 bytes starting at $BF00 are copied separately at $90D1.
Bitmap bytes copied to $E800-$EBFF by the page-copy call at $90C3. RAM is visible beneath I/O for this transfer.
Bitmap bytes copied to $EC00-$EFFF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
Bitmap bytes copied to $F000-$F3FF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
Bitmap bytes copied to $F400-$F7FF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
First 1024 bytes at the VIC bitmap base. The scene uses these directly, before the part copied from $D000 begins at $E800.
Next 1024 bytes already at the VIC bitmap base. The scene retains these below the start of the transfer destination at $E800.
